A user says Better Auth puts all auth data in your own DB with one CLI command, with no tie to a DB provider. It offers many features, such as OAuth login via Google, Apple and GitHub. They note it's free, versus paying for Supabase or Clerk.
Skeptic: "When I used it last year, I still found it lacking and it seemed to be run by one guy."

A user is setting up auth for a user app, client dashboards and internal tools. They needed anonymous users upgradable to real users, organizations, multi-tenancy and many sign-in options. They "haven't written a single line of special code," since included plugins and defaults handle it all, and they own all the data.

Comparing with Clerk: to support offline mobile auth they had to cache credentials and refresh tokens and pull tokens from undocumented Clerk keys. "This is supported by Better Auth out-of-the box. It doesn't hide these kinds of stuff from you."
"Better auth is great! I love how it's way more hackable than using something like Clerk." They added a plugin for auth via iframe postMessage (embedded in a CRM) and it worked seamlessly.
A user complains of a weird design where everything is "request header based." Running admin scripts and tests was very hacky because skipping that meant plugins wouldn't run.

BetterAuth supports email and password out of the box. NextAuth instead has a disclaimer that email/password is insecure and leaves you to implement password hashing yourself. "BetterAuth seems to be a bit more developer-focused."

A consultant used Better Auth to build client MVPs and likes its flexibility in designing the system around auth. Adding a per-user field is just a new Postgres column, versus using an API to append user data in Cognito/Auth0/Okta in a rigid format.
"I'm using it in production apps... IMO it's the best open-source option for a TypeScript developer who wants to implement authentication." The user also thanks the team for documenting it so well.
"better-auth is a joy to use. great dx with the type-safe plugin system... the quality of the lib and the docs is really high."
A team found better-auth immediately a better experience than other TypeScript auth libraries. There was no Next.js lock-in: they migrated from Next.js to Hono and only had to change the router.

A user reported a security vulnerability. Within 24 hours it was patched, a notice was posted, and they were credited with a CVE. They also say the library is more flexible than others and easier to wrap their head around.

A user migrated from Lucia: "it just works," and migration was easy using the CLI to generate tables. A quirk is that the auth client handles everything instead of giving server-side helper functions for login/register. They had to restructure login error handling around what the client returns.

Ex-Lucia user: they loved Lucia's total control, but are starting to like Better Auth's 'magic.' Email verification, password resets and rate limiting, which they dreaded coding, come built-in or as simple plugins.

"i really loved better-auth's DX but the nature of their database adapters means it's relatively easy to switch over to another provider/library". The user is concerned about Vercel adding cloud reliance after the acquisition.
A user says Better Auth does more than next-auth/auth.js: authn/z, acting as an identity provider and OIDC/SSO provider, RBAC, SAML/SCIM. They note some of those features are enterprise only.
"Better auth is an absolute dumpster fire codebase."

Better Auth makes adding passkeys take 7 lines of server code with virtually no client API change, versus Microsoft's lengthy .NET Core guide. "For ease-of-use and development speed, better-auth has been a clear winner for me."
"This framework has made auth such a non-issue for me. The setup is easy and the usage is consistent framework to framework."
A user wants to use Better Auth in an iOS app, but the client library is all JS. There is virtually no documentation on how to write their own client library.
